derived_results.claim: Deterministic finite-grid mixture optimization over a 13x13 Gaussian-null grid collapses numerically to the four rectangle corners, with total low-variance support about 0.554342 and high-variance support about 0.445658. This independently reinforces the r86 four-corner candidate.

Active-pair equalization across increasing deterministic quadrature orders gives rho converging through 0.55434204,0.55439904,0.55440559,0.55440972,0.55441136 toward the earlier r86 value near 0.55441744.

Exact second-derivative identities reduce full continuum validity to separate convexity of C(mu,log sigma): if C_mumu>=0 and C_tt>=0 everywhere, the maximum over the rectangular null set occurs at a corner, so four corner equalities close the RIPr KKT condition.

Deterministic quadrature/global search found minima C_mumu about 31.7 and C_tt about 54.8 with stable positive values as quadrature order increased. Interior C values are far below one. These margins make interval certification of derivatives much more attractive than direct near-corner certification of C.

negative_or_scope_evidence: No new value is adoption-grade: quadrature/global search is not directed-rounding or interval certified.
Finite-grid support collapse does not prove continuum support optimality.
Separate convexity is a proof route, not yet a proved property; promotion remains blocked on uniform positivity of both second derivatives.
All claims remain confined to the r86 standardized frozen NIG predictor and iid Gaussian null rectangle.
